turns.response_markdown: Tides are the regular rises and falls of ocean water caused mainly by the Moon’s gravity pulling on Earth’s oceans, with the Sun also contributing. As Earth rotates, different places move through these water bulges, creating high and low tides. Most coastlines experience two high tides and two low tides each day, though local geography can change this pattern. Tides influence marine ecosystems, navigation, and coastal activities. Their timing varies because the Moon’s position changes daily. Understanding tides helps people predict shoreline conditions and understand how Earth’s oceans respond naturally.
